generator.prompt: A goat of a Roman town market, mid-3rd century AD, standing square: all four legs straight and vertical, evenly spaced, head held level and facing forward, short tail held up, symmetrical. Realistic proportions, anatomically accurate. Single isolated model with complete geometry from every side and a bold, solid, readable silhouette from above. No ground plane, no display plinth, no text or inscriptions, no modern objects, no fantasy elements.

review.scope: Tripo's own render, four views of the final compressed model with a 1.8 m figure for scale (scripts/assets/preview-model.mjs), and the camps in the desktop build at High
review.notes: Mottled dark brown all over rather than patched brown and black, with no pale belly; otherwise as asked: backswept horns, a small beard, upright ears, its tail held up and a thin collar, 1.20 m long and 0.95 m to its horn tips. Two of it stand by Chapter II's woodpile, in the rain, and by the market stall in Chapters IX and XI: small, but goats at once by their horns and beards.
